question_type: Mean absolute deviation of 12 monthly receipts-by-source values over one FISCAL year

opus_path.decision: FY2018 = federal fiscal year Oct 2017 - Sep 2018 (12 months); series = FFO-2 net excise taxes, monthly, nominal, $ millions; MAD = mean of |x - mean|; 3 decimals.
The December issue after the fiscal year closes is the one issue that covers all of FY2018 -> Dec 2018 issue.
FFO-2 continued, column 'Excise taxes con. Net excise taxes (35)', monthly rows Oct..Sept plus the FY2018 annual / year-to-date rows.
Checked column alignment by summing the excise components in the first half of the table.

Compared col 35 across the Mar/Jun/Sep 2018 and Mar-Dec 2019 issues: a Dec-2017/Jan-2018 reallocation appears from the Dec 2018 printing on (same two-month sum); all other months identical; used the latest vintage.
calc.py asserts 12 values and that they sum to the printed FY2018 total, then computes the MAD (plus alternative definitions and the early vintage for the log).
Cross-checked Q4 against the narrative and the fourth-quarter receipts table.

opus_key_moves: Resolved FY2018 to Oct 2017 - Sep 2018 and took the December 2018 issue, whose window is exactly that fiscal year
Asserted that the 12 monthly values sum to the table's own FY2018 annual row, which guarantees the right 12 months
Ran a cross-vintage check and took the latest revision

first_divergence.what_glm_did: Read FFO-2 col 35 in the March 2019 issue, whose window runs Dec 2017 .. Dec 2018, and took the twelve rows Jan-Dec 2018 as 'FY2018 monthly' ([26] 'We have FY2018 monthly Jan-Dec net excise taxes'). That set is calendar 2018: it includes Oct-Dec 2018 (FY2019 months) and leaves out Oct-Dec 2017.
first_divergence.what_opus_did: Took Oct 2017 .. Sep 2018 from the December 2018 issue and asserted the sum equals the printed FY2018 annual row.
first_divergence.why_glm_went_that_way: It believed the March issue after the year holds the fiscal year ([26] 'For FY2018 monthly, March 2019 issue prints all FY2018 months') and never converted FY2018 into a month range; in the flattened window the rows after '2018 - Jan' simply read Jan..Dec. It then applied the calendar-month-span vintage cards C030/C031 and C032 (cited at [26]), which frame the task as calendar months.
first_divergence.consequence: Three fiscal-2019 months, including a large October, replaced three fiscal-2018 months, so the MAD is >60% too high.

secondary_errors.note: The FY2018 annual row of the same column was printed in the [25] output (treasury_bulletin_2019_03.txt:631), but it never compared its 12-month sum with that row. The sum differs from the annual row by a large margin, so the check would have exposed the wrong month set at once.
Its 'latest printing' sweep over the Jun/Sep/Dec 2019 issues ([28]-[34]) re-confirmed the wrong (calendar-2018) months as unrevised; the vintage work was diligent but aimed at the wrong period.

saw_correct_evidence.where: [25] printed the March 2019 FFO-2 window, which contains Dec 2017 and Jan-Sep 2018 (10 of the 12 FY2018 months) plus the FY2018 annual total row; it never read the Dec 2018 issue's FFO-2 (it only got a narrative search hit on 2018_12 at [17]).

glm_expressed_doubt.where: [26] 'likely these'; [37] doubts only about MAD about mean vs median and which receipts column, never about the month range.

operational.tool_friction: heredoc blocked [5],[19]; apply_patch unavailable [7],[9]; search() result shape confusion [12]-[16]; read() num_lines>150 rejected [21]; clipped outputs [24],[29],[31]
operational.notes: 75 s, 18 requests; friction was fixed quickly and did not cause the error.

adapter_context.relevant_item: none directly; the actor cited C032 (net budget receipts, calendar years) and C030 (calendar-year monthly spans, FFO-5) at [26]; C031 (FFO-3 calendar-month spans) is also in the deck
adapter_context.notes: No card covers fiscal-year month windows in FFO-2. Three cards in the deck are about CALENDAR-month spans; the actor used C030's vintage policy ('latest March/June/Sept/Dec issue printing each month') out of scope. The month-set error ('FY2018 monthly Jan-Dec') appears at the start of [26], before the cards are cited, so the cards reinforced rather than caused it.

remedies.intervention: Components-sum-to-annual check: when N monthly cells of a fiscal year are extracted and the table prints that fiscal year's annual or 'Fiscal year to date' row, assert sum(months) equals it (within rounding) before computing any statistic.
remedies.why: Opus built exactly this assert (calc.py), and the prompt arm caught its own identical mislabel at [34] by doing this sum. The annual row was already on screen in the cards arm's [25] output.

remedies.intervention: Month-resolved extractor returning (year, month, value) with year labels propagated, plus a period resolver 'FY2018 -> 2017-10 .. 2018-09' that selects exactly those keys and lists which issue prints all of them (the December issue).
remedies.why: The failure is choosing the wrong 12 rows in a flattened window; with explicit keys and a resolved FY range, calendar rows cannot pass as fiscal rows.

remedies.intervention: Convention card: 'FY N = Oct N-1 .. Sep N. FFO-2 December issues carry exactly one fiscal year of months; March issues carry Dec..Dec (a calendar year). Before computing, write the 12 (year, month) keys and check their sum against the FY annual row.'
remedies.why: The prompt arm had this as L-ffo2-receipts-by-source text ('Oct..Sep monthlies complete only in the December bulletin', AGENTS.md:253-258, 1363-1378) and still made the same mislabel at [15]; it recovered only through its own re-read and sum check at [34]. Text helps but the check does the work.

right_arms_note: none: stated at [9] that FY2018 = Oct 2017 - Sep 2018 and read the Dec 2018 FFO-2 window directly [11]-[14]; a clean principled path. prompt: made the SAME mislabel as cards at [13]-[15] (treated Oct-Dec 2018 of the March 2019 issue as revisions of FY2018 months) and computed the wrong-period value at [31]. At [34] it re-read the Dec 2018 window labels ('So Oct row is Oct 2017, not Oct 2018! Ah! I misread'), checked that the 12 months sum to the FY annual row, and committed the correct series at [35]/[39]. A self-caught near-miss, helped by its L-ffo2 lesson about December bulletins.
text_vs_mechanism: Needs a mechanism. The prompt arm had the right text (Oct..Sep monthlies complete only in the December bulletin) and still mislabelled the months; it was saved by an ad hoc sum-to-annual check, which the cards arm never ran. A mandatory months-sum-to-annual CHECK (and/or a year-month keyed extractor) would have caught the cards arm deterministically.
notes: This is the same year-label inheritance weakness seen in ordinal 14 (both wrong arms mislabelled Oct-Dec rows there too). It is systematic for this actor: flattened FFO windows print the year only on the first row of each year block, and the actor assigns the rows under it to the wrong year. It deserves a dedicated TOOL + CHECK pair rather than more lessons. Keyword-triggered cards about calendar-month spans (C030/C031/C032) are risky next to fiscal-year questions that share words like 'net budget receipts' and 'months'.
